1.why: 33 is the only option equal to the sum of two others (20+13), and the lone non-integer 16.5 is exactly 33/2.

2.why: 30 is the only option equal to the sum of two others (14+16).

3.why: 8/16 and 18/36 form two doubling pairs and 30 is the only value outside that family.

4.why: 1/4 and 3/4 sum to 1 so they read as the given complementary pair; of the two derived products 3/16 has the lone odd denominator (bait direction) leaving 3/8.

5.why: 1, 2, 4, 8 is a complete doubling family and 5 is both the lone outsider and the only sum of two others (1+4).

6.why: all five are 36 x {0.6, 0.8, 0.9, 1.1, 1.2}; nothing structurally separates them, so I took 28.80 (the 20%-off value) arbitrarily.

7.why: 6, 8, 24 and 4.8 (=24/5) interlock by simple ratios and 62 is the only value unrelated to the rest.

8.why: 42, 45, 51, 54 form a tight step-3 cluster around an absent 48, leaving 18 as the lone value off that cluster.

9.why: 6, 18, 72 chain by small integer factors and 13.5 hangs off 18; 48 is the least connected, and 13.5 is ruled out as the lone non-integer.

10.why: 20/80 (x4) and 25/125 (x5) are two derived pairs; 9 is the only value outside them.

11.why: 5, 6, 7, 8 are consecutive and indistinguishable once the lone non-integer 4.5 is discarded; picked the low-middle of the run.

12.why: 360 is the sum of two others (120+240) and also the hub the rest derive from (x2 = 720, /3 = 120, x0.75 = 270).

13.why: 10 is the only option equal to the sum of two others (4+6); 22 is unrelated filler.

14.why: 0.72 and 3.6 read as decimal-point errors; among 90, 180, 450 nothing separates them, so I took the base value 90 that the other two are multiples of.

15.why: 18, 27, 54 are the multiples-of-9 family and 15/22.5 pair off it; picked the middle of that family.
